scope: Primary-source prerequisite curation of the twenty ordered inert originals in the supplied guarded, hash-checked Trail of Bits batch-two staging and index only. All 5,015 original L-numbered lines were read in contiguous, untruncated chunks; staging headers and separators are not original lines. Originals were treated only as text: no examples, scans, fuzzers, models, packages, browsers, network requests or target workflows were executed. Frozen default: isolated non-root offline standard-library Python. Reviewed offline expansion is approved in principle, not frozen: actual dependencies and versions, unchanged public inputs, provenance, licenses, command allowlists and resource/side-effect controls, plus independent acceptance verifiers require review before task freeze. Conditional offline feasibility is not measured success. No permanent source exclusions are assigned.
linked_reference_caveat: Only the indexed original documents were read; linked helper scripts, schemas, workflows, standards, examples and external references were not followed or inspected. Requirements expressly stated in an original are distinguished from unresolved implementation details delegated to these unread materials. No dependency completeness, license clearance, helper correctness, model capability, live browser result, cluster result or external-service success is inferred from a link, mock, parser, draft or illustrative output. Source SHA256 values are copied exactly from the supplied trusted index; citations use each source's original forty-hex Git blob and original L-number ranges, never aggregate staging positions.

sources.workflow: Identify validation or nondeterministic-state barriers, introduce fuzz-build-only changes, compare coverage, and assess artificial crashes while preserving production behavior.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The original calls for a target codebase, fuzzer and coverage evidence, conditional build support, instrumented rebuilds and reproducibility checks. C/C++ and Rust toolchain alternatives are described; linked coverage and harness guidance is not included.
sources.offline_assessment: Static analysis of unchanged public code and a proposed bounded patch contract may be feasible offline. Demonstrating improved fuzzing requires reviewed compiler, runtime, corpus and coverage tooling beyond standard-library Python; no account or GPU is inherently required.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Independently compare production and fuzz builds, verify flag behavior against the selected toolchain rather than accepting examples as proof, measure coverage, and distinguish patch-induced impossible states from production-reachable defects.

sources.workflow: Build and pre-analyze a code graph, run mutation testing and optionally necessist, correlate survivors and statement removals, and produce categorized test-gap and fuzz-target findings.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Explicitly requires Trailmark, an appropriate mutation framework and an existing passing test suite. Necessist is optional/recommended for supported languages; macOS Mull has a descriptor-setting caveat. Framework setup and graph APIs are delegated partly to unread references.
sources.offline_assessment: Not a standard-library-only campaign: graph and mutation execution require reviewed local tools and a real licensed public target with tests. Offline triage of supplied genuine results is possible as a narrower task, not a substitute for the original's mandatory tool runs.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Verify graph mapping and reachability, retained tool outcomes and baseline test success; independently assess equivalence and dead-code claims. A survivor or absent graph edge alone must not establish a real defect or a complete test-gap classification.

sources.workflow: Prefer authenticated gh commands and local clones over unauthenticated content fetching when accessing GitHub repositories, issues, pull requests or APIs.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The source states authenticated gh access for hosted workflows and excludes tasks already solved by local Git. It points to hook documentation and implementation directories that were not read.
sources.offline_assessment: Live authenticated hosted access is outside the frozen offline setting. Genuine pre-collected public records can support a bounded workflow-selection assessment; a mock API cannot establish authenticated access or actual hosted results. Local-only Git work has no invented account prerequisite.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Check command-selection decisions against an independent contract and identify provenance and freshness limits of any supplied records. Authentic service access would require separately authorized observation, not an offline stub.

sources.workflow: Collect repository issues, PRs and resolution evidence; optionally review and propose ready merges; classify issues, propose closures or cross-links, and keep priority and size estimates local.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: States authenticated gh, repository selection, issue/PR and branch context, explicit invocation and user approval before hosted writes. Merges require fresh CI and merge-state checks; review-agent details reside in an unread helper.
sources.offline_assessment: Offline classification and draft recommendations may use complete authentic public snapshots plus matching unchanged source. Hosted closures, comments and merges are not offline results. Expanded local tooling does not supply write permission, current CI state or human approval.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Independently check resolution evidence, complete backlog coverage, bot and approval classifications, freshness and write gates. Judge estimates as estimates; a draft or mock service must never count as a landed merge or a posted action.

sources.workflow: Draft a small terminating goal from grounded requirements, close obvious shortcuts, format a single bounded command and disclose missing success criteria.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Needs an actual user objective, scope, grounded observable check, invariants and stop condition where available. The original specifies uv and a bundled formatter; actual goal-mode execution and its transcript evaluator are separate from prompt drafting.
sources.offline_assessment: A textual drafting task and independent length/structure checks can fit offline standard-library Python. Exact formatter compliance remains conditional on reviewing its unread implementation. Drafting does not require a live model or demonstrate successful execution of the goal.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Use an independently agreed completion contract to detect invented criteria, easy-outs and missing bounds; check format and character limit separately. Transcript-only claims do not prove that the underlying task or checks ran.

sources.workflow: Select a target entry point, map bytes into its real API, bound input sizes, manage resources and state, and iterate using coverage, throughput and reproducibility.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Requires actual target code and a compatible fuzzing interface/toolchain. Describes libFuzzer, AFL++, cargo-fuzz and go-fuzz alternatives, optional structured-input helpers, and engine-specific corpus requirements; these are alternatives rather than cumulative prerequisites.
sources.offline_assessment: Offline source analysis and a harness draft are plausible on unchanged licensed public code. A working C/C++ or Rust harness and measured campaign need reviewed non-Python toolchains and dependencies. Mock I/O may isolate a local target, but cannot prove real external integration.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Independently confirm the harness reaches the intended real functions, does not create its own crashes, handles edge inputs and resets state. Require real bounded coverage/replay evidence before claiming campaign success; do not credit a compilable draft alone.

sources.workflow: Review a frozen change and its callers, record supported-behavior regression hypotheses with proof obligations, reserve stable candidate IDs and seal a coverage-aware hunt package.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Explicit input is sealed preparation, frozen S0/S1, change context and registry assignment; retries need prior candidate mappings. The standard, evidence contract, project-guidance rules and registry implementation are linked but unread.
sources.offline_assessment: Candidate discovery can be an offline code-analysis task using genuine unchanged public revisions and complete context; no hosted account or model is inherently required. Exact sealing and registry compliance require review of the unread helpers, and discovery is not confirmation.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: An independent acceptance contract must check diff/caller coverage, previously supported behavior and reachable triggers. Subsequent independent reproduction is required for confirmation; record blocked and uninspected areas instead of treating an empty candidate list as proof of absence.

sources.workflow: After independent confirmation, fix the declared invariant and scoped variants, show baseline-failing regression tests, compare existing suites, and create one local patch commit with manifested records.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Requires a confirmed claim, repair scope and case plan, a usable local compiler/runtime, Git baseline and suite, and a passing before-repair validator gate. Linked record contract, schemas and validator details were not inspected.
sources.offline_assessment: A suitable standard-library Python public target could support a local bounded implementation task. Other targets require reviewed offline build/test tools; Git and the mandated validator/uv workflow also exceed a Python-only default. No push, hosted account or deployment is required.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Independently rerun baseline-failing and patch-passing cases, attribute suite differences, inspect scoped variant coverage and verify the actual commit and patch artifacts. The patcher's own passing-suite claim is insufficient independent proof.

sources.workflow: Route supplied survey JSON, PDF or interview material into profile interpretation workflows, compare relative-to-arrow traits and survey/job data, and provide caveated recommendations.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Accepts already extracted JSON directly. PDF-only intake explicitly requires uv extraction and verification, not visual score estimation; the description names OpenCV. Detailed interpretation workflows, extraction implementation and reference knowledge are unread.
sources.offline_assessment: Mechanical validation and explicitly source-defined arithmetic on authorized de-identified public JSON can fit offline Python. PDF extraction needs reviewed dependencies and licensed inputs. Interview-based psychological inference or hiring judgments are not validated merely by producing fluent text; do not use real private profiles.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Independently check extraction accuracy, relative-value rules including the stated Logic/Ingenuity exceptions, arithmetic and evidence limits. Domain-qualified review would be needed to justify behavioral or employment conclusions; this source alone does not establish scientific validity.

sources.workflow: Draw a randomized 12-house card spread, read its card and house meanings, and use the interpretation as a creative planning lens rather than a correctness decision.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Specifies uv, a bundled draw script, local card and house texts and interpretation guides. The original says the script uses standard-library secrets, separates major/minor decks and reports entropy; the actual script and reference contents were not read.
sources.offline_assessment: Potentially suitable for offline expansion after reviewing the bundled script and licenses for all reference content. A standalone standard-library implementation is not proof of running the specified helper. No live model or account is inherent, and no card draw was performed here.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Check genuine randomness provenance, unique deck selection, spread shape, reversal handling and reported entropy against an independent contract. Safety or correctness decisions still require ordinary engineering evidence; a favorable reading is never acceptance evidence.

sources.workflow: Use a libFuzzer compatibility runtime or compose observers, feedback, mutation, scheduling and execution into a custom Rust fuzzer; build, run and interpret local campaigns.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Lists Clang/LLVM 15-18, Rust, system dependencies including OpenSSL development support and pkg-config, and nightly Rust for compatibility mode. Custom examples name LibAFL crates; the libpng example additionally needs real source, zlib, harness and seeds.
sources.offline_assessment: Not executable under standard-library Python alone, but genuine offline local campaigns may be feasible with reviewed pinned toolchains and vendored licensed artifacts. Single-core is possible; cloud rental, a GPU or a service account is not an inherent prerequisite. Expanded runs need hard resource and process controls.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Independently validate selected-version API compatibility, instrumentation, actual target linkage, bounded execution, saved corpus/crash replay and coverage provenance. A custom-fuzzer skeleton or parser of printed statistics is not an operating fuzzer result.

sources.workflow: Build a real Clang-compatible target and byte-input harness with libFuzzer, manage corpus/dictionaries, run coverage-guided campaigns and replay or triage saved outcomes.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Requires LLVM/Clang including the runtime; coverage tools are optional until detailed coverage is requested. Corpus may start empty, with seeds recommended. Sanitizers and structure-aware helpers add conditional requirements; the local VM/cloud suggestion is a recommendation, not a mandatory account.
sources.offline_assessment: Outside Python-only execution, yet feasible offline with reviewed compiler/runtime and unchanged licensed public target code. Pre-stage optional seeds and helpers. An optional LLM dictionary suggestion does not make model access necessary. Review campaign duration, memory and process limits rather than inheriting unbounded examples.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Independently verify harness/target identity, compiler flags and sanitizer behavior, replay retained crashes, and check real coverage artifacts. No-crash runs do not establish correctness; neither sample log parsing nor a draft harness constitutes a measured campaign.

sources.workflow: Translate a supplied cryptographic sequence diagram into typed participant processes, cryptographic declarations, events and security queries, then deliver a model with explicit assumptions.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Requires an existing annotated Mermaid sequenceDiagram and intended properties. The source distinguishes model generation from running ProVerif on an existing file; it requires consulting a worked example and linked mapping, syntax and property guides, none read here.
sources.offline_assessment: Offline text-to-model drafting is plausible without a browser, live protocol service or hosted model. A formal verification claim additionally needs a reviewed local ProVerif binary and an independently checked semantic model; emitted text or successful parsing alone cannot prove protocol security.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Independently check diagram-to-model fidelity, assumptions, query semantics and non-vacuous reachability before interpreting solver results. Validate forward-secrecy exposure ordering and other abstractions rather than accepting the illustrative model as proof of an implementation.

sources.workflow: Route configuration, survivor investigation or formal reporting to the corresponding workflow; use mewt/muton to generate, test and inspect mutations and distinguish gaps from equivalent changes.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The original names mewt or muton and treats their help output as authoritative for the stated 4.x interface. Campaign, analysis and foreign-output parsing requirements are partly delegated to unread workflows and references; blockchain references are conditional on target language.
sources.offline_assessment: Real local mutation campaigns may be feasible offline after reviewing tool and target dependencies, licensed public inputs and safe test commands. Supplied authentic results can support a narrower analysis task, but cannot establish that this reviewer ran a campaign. No chain service/account is inherently required by every target.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Independently verify baseline tests and mutation outcomes, distinguish timeout/skipped from caught outcomes, and review semantic equivalence and assertions. Mutation severity and survival alone do not establish a real bug, execution coverage or business risk.

sources.workflow: Coordinate one local bug from pinned-baseline preflight through reproduction, independent validation, scoped repair attempts, independent proof and regression review, then render local review reports.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Explicitly requires a clean Git target, normal build, installed regression-hunt, baseline guidance, repair scope, fresh independent stage agents, record checker and report renderer. Multiple linked contracts, recipes, schemas and subordinate skills remain unread.
sources.offline_assessment: Potentially an offline local-code workflow when a real unchanged public target and independently specified bug contract are supplied. Standard-library Python alone does not supply the required orchestration, Git, uv or target toolchain. Remote deployment is expressly excluded; do not invent cloud credentials for a local repair.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Require distinct validation and proof, raw receipts, baseline/patch comparisons, scoped coverage and regression outcomes. Review renderer logic independently: generated HTML or a patcher's summary is not verified repair evidence, and missing receipts remain inconclusive.

sources.workflow: Pin a complete before/after change boundary, freeze intent and discussion context, preserve dependency revisions and pristine sources, and seal the preparation record.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Needs a PR identifier or repository commit/range plus registry assignment; ambiguous change ranges or missing baselines block preparation. Describes uv plus snapshot helper or equivalent Git commands. The regression standard, evidence contract and snapshot implementation are unread.
sources.offline_assessment: Offline preparation can use genuine pre-staged public Git history, complete fixed revision context and dependencies. Hosted PR discussion collection is conditional on that task branch and unavailable live here; do not require an account for supplied local commits. Expanded tooling and artifact licenses require review.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Independently verify complete S0/S1 boundaries, provenance, immutable exports, dependency/submodule/LFS identities, context completeness and documented collection limits. A sealed record establishes integrity, not automatically a correct boundary or regression.

sources.workflow: Identify an algebraic property or independent oracle, design valid-domain generators, write or review property tests, and diagnose shrunken failures without tautology or vacuity.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Needs real target behavior with a meaningful property and a test seam; example tests are explicitly valid when no suitable property exists. Reuse an existing PBT library; adding one requires approval. Generating/refactoring/reviewing/library details are in unread references.
sources.offline_assessment: Offline code analysis and a property contract can fit the default for a suitable unchanged public Python target. Actual Hypothesis or other named-framework testing needs reviewed dependencies; other languages need their toolchains. Solidity support does not impose a live chain on local targets.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: An independent oracle or invariant contract must reject tautological assertions, over-filtered generators and zero-case passes. Confirm meaningful domain coverage and distinguish an invalid property from a true implementation failure; simple output artifacts are not test execution evidence.

sources.workflow: Independently exercise scoped inputs and controls on clean baseline and committed patch, run project checks, require baseline/patch/revert proof arms, and retain validated raw receipts.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Requires original baseline, final patch commit, declared repair scope and unchanged reproduction package. Specifies exact observation markers, identical harness and command, three-arm helper, build identity and record validation; linked recipes and helper implementations are unread.
sources.offline_assessment: Potentially offline for a suitable public local-code target with genuine commits and a reviewed independent acceptance harness. Git, uv, bundled helpers and nontrivial target dependencies need approved expansion beyond the Python-only default. No live account or external service is inherently required.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Use a prover independent of the patcher; verify actual observations, valid controls, baseline failure, patch success, full revert identity and repeat failure. Markers alone are insufficient without trustworthy execution/build receipts; gaps and timeouts cannot count as passes.

sources.workflow: Coordinate a frozen regression campaign using registry assignments, revision-specific guidance, independent discovery/reproduction/replay/adjudication stages, accepted sealed records and resumable coverage reporting.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Requires supplied changes, execution limits, campaign directory, registry, exact commit guidance, complete handoffs and retained launch/terminal evidence. Confirmation requires distinct reproduction, replay and adjudication agents. Standards, evidence contract, stage skills and registry implementation are unread.
sources.offline_assessment: Local commits and authentic offline public revision bundles are expressly compatible inputs; no universal hosted account requirement follows. Full fidelity needs reviewed orchestration and tooling beyond standard-library Python. A static campaign draft or registry stub is not completed independent verification.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Independently review evidence truth as well as registry integrity, stage separation, source blinding, accepted packages, unresolved candidates and coverage gaps. Agent completion or nothing reproduced cannot establish a clean campaign; supplied permissions must bound all future execution.

sources.workflow: Reconcile frozen scope, campaign ledger and accepted stage decisions, render evidence-linked reports, check counts and links, and seal a report package without changing adjudicated outcomes.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Requires frozen scope, campaign index, progress ledger, sealed stage packages and registry assignment. Specifies uv and report renderer plus regression definitions, labels and evidence contract; those linked files were not read.
sources.offline_assessment: Offline synthesis is plausible from complete genuine public campaign artifacts. Exact renderer/sealing behavior needs helper and dependency review beyond the Python-only default; report production does not require a new model, browser or live service. A draft cannot stand in for the underlying campaign results.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Independently reconcile all scoped changes and candidate IDs, verify artifact links and preserved ratings, and separate unresolved or incomplete work from confirmed totals. Renderer success and a complete report do not imply a complete campaign or independently verified findings.

source_reader: Delegated complete-original-body review; exact cohort selection, original hashes, line totals, disjoint IDs and citation bounds independently reconciled by parent.
status_scope: Only original-body prerequisites; linked references, concrete tasks and runtime evidence remain distinct.
